mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 5% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor market strengthening events, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (quantile regression slope < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as it signals resilient economic demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in at least 70% of similar demand cycles (backtested quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds the Fed's target range by more than 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days tends to be negative due to anticipated tightening.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_prev_month + 0.5pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 80% of such inflation surprises, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in residential housing starts (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a dual signal of demand and liquidity, predicting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by at least 0.1 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a control period (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly payrolls increase (PAYEMS) but the unemployment rate remains above 4%, it indicates labor market expansion without wage pressure, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE > 4.0% for the current month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of such labor expansions (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in the ratio of retail sales (not available in the catalog; fallback: use GDPC1 as proxy for broad demand) of at least 8% suggests weakening demand, predicting a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by at least 8% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically lower than the prior 5-day average in 70% of similar events (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month moving average of industrial production (INDPRO_12MA) falls below its previous month's value for three consecutive months, it indicates softening supply conditions, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO_12MA_prev_month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically more negative than in baseline periods (t-test p > 0.05).
